transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2025-05-15
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 55 min
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Jasper O'Neil (Redwood SE), Ravi Singh (Redwood SE), Ellen Park (Galen Procurement), Drew Kapoor (Galen Security), Samir Patel (Galen Platform Eng), Lena Ortiz (Galen Legal)

Summary (auto): Procurement and security focused pre-onboarding. Primary concerns: KMS key ownership, SSO/SAML integration, DPA/MsA exceptions, dedicated capacity pricing commitments.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um this is Maya from Redwood, i've got Jasper and Ravi with me. you all good on audio?
[00:14] Ellen: yep, hi, thanks — we have the procurement squad oncall, plus Drew for security and Samir for the infra questions.
[00:27] Maya: great. quick agenda: walk through the onboarding path, MSA/DPA items we've seen most often, KMS options and SSO, and then pricing/commits for Dedicated. leave time at the end for next steps. sound OK?
[00:41] Drew: yes, we can run. Our big thing is keying and audit logs — we need to know if keys ever leave our control, and what the egress paths look like.
[00:53] Jasper: understood. we support both Redwood-managed KMS and customer-managed keys with cloud KMS integrations; also we have an HSM-anchored option for private deployments — some folks say HMS, we mean HSM — apologies if the auto-transcript mangled that earlier.
[01:12] Samir: can you clarify the difference? like we have a policy requiring customer-owned keys for PII in prod. if RW holds the keys, is there a key escrow?
[01:24] Jasper: good q. with customer-managed keys (CMK) we never have plaintext access to the root key. we use envelope encryption: your cloud KMS wraps the dataset-level keys. Redwood keeps only the encrypted blobs; to perform inference the service requests unwrapping from the cloud KMS in your VPC — there's an option to deploy the control plane in your VPC for extra assurance.
[01:45] Drew: okay, so the unwrap call stays inside our VPC? that matters for our compliance.
[01:51] Jasper: it can — for Private deployments we run the control plane in your VPC, yes. for Hosted we offer customer KMS integration but the call traverses our control plane unless you pick private.
[02:05] Ellen: what's the SLA difference between Hosted and Dedicated? procurement will ask about credits for missed latency SLOs.
[02:12] Maya: Hosted is our standard offering — flexible, pay-as-you-go. Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and an SLA for uptime and per-request p99 latency target we can negotiate in the contract. SLA credits are included in Dedicated tiers.
[02:29] Lena: on the MSA/DPA front, are there typical exceptions customers ask for? what should we expect to redline?
[02:36] Maya: common asks: audit-log retention windows, subprocessor lists, limited liability caps, and data residency clauses. on the DPA side, some customers request deletion confirmations and a stronger egress/migration clause. we'll send prior redline examples.
[02:53] Lena: and is Redwood open to an addendum for our internal security controls mapping? we need a table that maps Redwood controls to our SOC2/ISO control numbers.
[03:01] Ravi: yes, we provide a control-mapping workbook. i'll include it in the package.
[03:08] Samir: performance question — our product depends on low tail latency. what typical 99p numbers do you hit for a 8k-context model?
[03:17] Jasper: depends on model, quantization, and batch policy. for a 8k seq on a 4-GPU Dedicated shard with optimized kernels we see p99s in the 180-250ms range for smaller models, larger models stretch higher. if you need <100ms p99 we usually recommend model-choice + shorter contexts or sharding across lower-latency instances.
[03:39] Samir: hmm, our target is 200ms p99 for the main inference path. that seems achievable?
[03:44] Jasper: yes, achievable with Dedicated and tuned batching; we'll propose a config in the PoC.
[03:49] Ellen: pricing — procurement will ask for committed vs on-demand rates. what's typical for a month's reserve?
[03:56] Maya: we do monthly/annual reserved capacity contracts. pricing scales with GPU class and concurrency. i can share a cost worksheet — example ranges: light commit (small pool) reduces unit cost by ~20%, mid commit 30-40%, large commit up to 55% depending on usage profile. exact numbers depend on model mix.
[04:20] Ellen: can you share a sample worksheet? we need it for our TCO and to present to finance.
[04:24] Maya: absolutely. Jasper will build an initial estimate given a traffic profile.
[04:30] Samir: we'll share a 7-day sample of requests and token counts. is that enough?
[04:34] Jasper: yes that's perfect. we also want a list of peak qps windows.
[04:38] Drew: on encryption and logs — we need audit logs tied to user IDs and key-access events for 12 months. do you support that?
[04:46] Ravi: we stream audit logs to customer S3 or to their SIEM via secure transfer. retention is configurable; 12 months is common.
[04:54] Drew: ok, good. what about RBAC and role separation? our ops team must not be able to view customer plaintext.
[04:59] Jasper: RBAC is supported; we can integrate with your SSO via SAML/SCIM for provisioning. internal support teams operate on redacted telemetry; full content access requires explicit escalation and is audited.
[05:15] Lena: DPA question — do you allow subprocessor restriction? we have a list of disallowed subprocessors.
[05:21] Maya: we publish our subprocessor list; for certain enterprise customers we can consider contractual restrictions, subject to procurement review.
[05:30] Ellen: procurement timeline — we need to get pricing and DPA redline into our vendor gate by May 23. is that feasible?
[05:36] Maya: yes, if we share docs today and you return redlines by 21st we can make the 23rd gate.
[05:41] Lena: we'll try, but legal may need two cycles.
[05:45] Maya: noted.
[05:48] Samir: one blocker — our security team has a strict rule: no outbound calls to third-party key management endpoints unless whitelisted. would Redwood be able to run the KMS unwrap within our VPC?
[05:59] Jasper: yes for Private deployment. For Dedicated in Redwood tenant, the unwrap will be to your KMS endpoint over our secure link; if strict network segmentation is required, Private gives full inbound-only controls.
[06:14] Drew: any differences for on-prem? we might run some workloads on-prem for PHI.
[06:19] Jasper: On-prem package exists — it's a separate offering with local control plane. there are additional engineering and license steps; we can scope that after procurement.
[06:31] Ellen: what about data residency? we need EU data to remain in EU.
[06:35] Maya: you can pin deployment region; Dedicated/Private can guarantee region residency and we can include it in the SLI/SLA.
[06:44] Samir: competitor question: we've tried VendorX on-prem before and the ops overhead killed velocity. how much integration engineering should we expect?
[06:52] Maya: initial setup varies — hosting in your VPC or private on-prem has more upfront work but is well-documented. Redwood provides runbooks and a solutions engineering lead to minimize lift.
[07:04] Drew: procurement will want to know fallback: if a model or instance type is deprecated, what's the rollback?
[07:11] Jasper: we support rollout policies — canary, A/B, automatic fallback to cheaper variants. that's part of the deployment config.
[07:20] Ellen: ok — let's talk deliverables recap.
[07:23] Maya: recap: we'll send security pack + SOC2/ISO certs, a DPA redline summary, and Jasper will draft a PoC config + initial cost worksheet. Ellen will run procurement gate. Samir will provide traffic samples. Lena will annotate legal must-haves.
[07:40] Lena: question about indemnity — we have a clause preference around consumer-facing exposures. is Redwood flexible on that?
[07:46] Maya: we can review in the MSA negotiation. some items are deal-specific. we'll surface common compromises we've done.
[07:55] Samir: timeline — if procurement clears by 5/23 and legal by 5/28, can we start a PoC the week of 5/26?
[08:02] Maya: yes, target PoC kickoff the week of 5/26 works. Jasper: i'll block time.
[08:07] Ellen: great. a few quick clarifying notes — (1) procurement needs a single pricing table with both committed and on-demand lines; (2) security wants the KMS flow diagram; (3) legal wants the DPA annotated.
[08:20] Maya: we'll deliver those.
[08:23] Drew: one more — does Redwood support exporting full audit logs in a vendor-neutral format?
[08:28] Ravi: yes, export to S3/ELK/whatever you use. format is newline-json with event types.
[08:34] Ellen: ok thanks, that's helpful.
[08:36] Maya: any blockers remaining?
[08:38] Samir: none from eng beyond finalizing traffic sample.
[08:41] Lena: legal will try to get redlines in by the 21st but can't promise earlier.
[08:46] Ellen: procurement will schedule their gate 5/23.
[08:49] Maya: perfect. we'll follow up with the package within 24 hours. thanks all.
